Yes. The 2023 tree-cover loss is **corroborated under the tool’s rule** in the latest run: a later year was observed, and the JRC 2020 reference mapped 100% of the event area as forest, exceeding the 50% threshold.

The detected event covers **4.5 hectares**, or 0.12% of the property. Uruguay’s 2021 forest map classifies 4.3 hectares as planted pine forest and 0.2 hectares as outside mapped forest; none is mapped as native forest.

An additional 1.3 hectares of loss occurred in patches below the 0.5-hectare minimum and was not counted as an event. The earlier 2024 run did not yet meet the corroboration rule because no later year had been observed.
